idiom_name: Pekko Routers.pool / group router with pluggable routing logic
implementation_notes: Pekko (classically Akka) provides the router as a framework object: Routers.pool spawns routee children and a group router forwards to an ActorRef set discovered through the Receptionist, so the destination set is runtime state rather than compiled code. Routing logic is pluggable - round-robin by default, a broadcast predicate, or custom - and reconfiguration flows through supervisor behaviours and actor messages, which is the pattern's control channel in actor form. Use it when destinations are actors and the rule is which actor or group currently serves a message; for content routing inside a stream, prefer the functional variant.
pitfalls: A pool router's routees are local children, so a destination set cannot span the cluster - cluster-wide routing needs a group router plus the Receptionist.
Routee lifecycle is supervision-driven: a crashed routee is restarted and re-added, but a stopped one silently shrinks the pool, so a rule that assumes a specific routee can land on another.
A broadcast predicate that never matches turns the router into a plain pool, with the intended fan-out silently gone.

variants.name: Runtime-composed PartialFunction rule chain
variants.idiom_name: PartialFunction[Message, Destination] chain (orElse) swapped through an AtomicReference
variants.implementation_notes: The pure-Scala realization is a function from message to destination: rules are PartialFunction[Message, Destination] values composed with orElse into one router function that is rebuilt and published atomically (AtomicReference, or a stream stage rebuilt on change), with sealed traits and pattern matching making each rule's condition readable and exhaustive. This keeps routing testable as plain functions - no actor system needed in unit tests - and suits content-based decisions over plain callables; choose the router-object variant when destinations are actors that need supervision and a dispatch strategy.
pitfalls: orElse chains evaluate in order and cost O(n): index the chain (for example by message kind) before it grows, not after latency degrades.
isDefinedAt must be pure - a condition with side effects or a throwing match is evaluated twice and can behave differently the second time.
Publishing a new chain is not enough if a rule closes over stale state; publish new closures instead of mutating captured state.
